whatWeDo.heading: What We Do
whatWeDo.text: Quarterly ecosystem health surveys with WCS tracking coral, fish biomass, and seagrass across 15 years of data.
whatWeDo.text2: Supporting 18 Beach Management Units managing 120 km² of co-managed waters across Kilifi County.
whatWeDo.text3: Economic models, ecotourism concessions, and revenue strategies that keep conservation alive beyond donor cycles.
whatWeDo.text4: The Kuruwitu model works because it's backed by rigorous science, sustainable finance, and institutional support. Community-led doesn't mean community-alone. Oceans Alive provides the technical expertise, monitoring infrastructure, and evidence base that turns grassroots passion into policy-ready conservation.
whatWeDo.text5: In partnership with Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS), we conduct quarterly monitoring surveys that track ecosystem health across coral cover, fish biomass, and seagrass recovery. This isn't data for journals - it's proof that the model works. When the Royal Family visited Kuruwitu in 2023, when IUCN awarded the Blue Champions recognition in 2022, when Kenya's government endorsed the first Co-Management Plan - they did it because the evidence was undeniable.
whatWeDo.text6: This programme also generates the sustainable revenue models that keep conservation alive beyond donor cycles: economic assessments, business plans, aquatic ecotourism concessions with Vipingo Ridge and LEAP, grants from IUCN/EU BIOPAMA, and KCW-CBO revenue streams generating USD 10–20K annually. Conservation that doesn't pay for itself doesn't last.
whatWeDo.text7: Partnership with Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) | 15 Years of Data
whatWeDo.text8: In partnership with WCS, Oceans Alive conducts quarterly monitoring surveys that track the health of Kuruwitu's marine ecosystems. These aren't academic exercises - they're the proof that community-led conservation delivers measurable, long-term recovery. Fifteen years of data show a 400% increase in fish biomass, 30% reef recovery, 17% seagrass regrowth, and an 85% coral survival rate in restoration sites.
whatWeDo.text9: Catch Assessment Surveys (CAS) and Frame Surveys (FS) track fish abundance and diversity across the sanctuary and surrounding waters. The 400% biomass increase within the Tengefu LMMA and 135% improvement in surrounding catch prove that protected areas benefit fishers, not just fish.
whatWeDo.text10: Regular assessments measure coral cover, recruitment, and reef condition. An 85% survival rate in coral restoration sites demonstrates that community-led restoration isn't just symbolic - it's rebuilding reefs at scale, backed by science.
whatWeDo.text12: This monitoring data underpinned Kenya's first officially endorsed Co-Management Plan (2022), Kenya's first IUCN SAGE analysis, and the development of the 6-step co-management toolkit now being adopted across Kilifi County's 18 BMUs. Science didn't replace community wisdom - it amplified it.
whatWeDo.text13: Conservation that doesn't generate its own revenue doesn't survive. This programme develops the economic models that keep community-led conservation alive beyond project cycles: aquatic ecotourism concessions with Vipingo Ridge and LEAP, business plans for community-based organizations, and diversified funding from IUCN/EU BIOPAMA and other strategic partners.
whatWeDo.text19: Oceans Alive coordinates the Kilifi County BMU Network - 18 Beach Management Units managing 120 km² of co-managed waters. This isn't bureaucracy; it's how fisher voices reach county and national policy. We support BMUs in applying fisheries policies, developing co-management plans, and ensuring that community rights are recognized and protected.
whatWeDo.text25: In partnership with WCS, quarterly monitoring surveys track ecosystem health and conservation impact through Catch Assessment Surveys, Frame Surveys, and the State of Fishery 2021 report.
